title: Habitats
seo_title: Year 2 Science: Habitats Worksheets (Woodland, Pond, Seashore, Desert, Arctic)
standard_code: Year 2: Living things and their habitats
standard_text: Identify that most living things live in habitats to which they are suited and describe how different habitats provide for the basic needs of different kinds of animals and plants, and how they depend on each other. Identify and name a variety of plants and animals in their habitats.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on habitats: woodland, pond, seashore, ocean, desert and polar habitats, how animals are suited to them and counting animals. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A habitat is a natural home.
key_sub: It gives food, water and shelter. Animals are suited to their habitat.
body_html:
How to think about it

A habitat gives food, water and shelter.

  • Woodland, pond, seashore, ocean, desert and polar lands are habitats.
  • Living things are suited to their habitat.
  • In the wrong habitat, a living thing cannot get what it needs.
Example

Where does a camel live?

Hot and dry

Answer: a desert

Example

Why does a polar bear have thick fur?

Very cold place

Answer: to keep warm

Common mistakes

  • Thinking animals can live anywhere.
  • Thinking a habitat is just a house.
  • Thinking polar bears live with penguins.

faq.a: The natural home of a plant or animal. It gives the living thing the food, water and shelter it needs.

faq.q: Why do animals live in different habitats?
faq.a: Each animal is suited to its habitat. A fish has gills for water; a polar bear has thick fur for the cold.
Woodlands, ponds, the seashore, the ocean, deserts, rainforests and the icy Arctic and Antarctic are all habitats.
